name: UPENG lets anyone burn the pair's tokens
summary: UPENG (unverified) exposes burn(address,uint256) (0x9dc29fac) to any caller, burning from any account. The attacker's contract bought 13,955 UPENG with 0.001 BNB, burned all but 1 wei of the UPENG/WBNB pair's 20.99m UPENG, called sync() to set the UPENG reserve to 1 wei, and sold its UPENG into the pair for its entire 1.501 WBNB.
notes: The token's source is unverified; the mechanism is read from the anchor's trace, and an eth_call of burn(pair, 1e18) from an arbitrary address at the block before the anchor succeeds, so the function has no access check. Reset: deployment (29 minutes before the anchor); the deployer's only later calls were an approve and the addLiquidityETH that created the pair.

The anchor was the pair's first trade after the deployer's 1.5 WBNB liquidity, so no earlier exploit is possible; later transactions moved dust only. Loss is the pair's net WBNB outflow, which already nets the attacker's 0.001 BNB buy; the victim is the deployer's liquidity.
